answer: A work-backed reputation bond resists sybil attacks: each agent must forge a verifiable history by completing paid tasks and staking a deposit before it can trade. Creating one fake identity is cheap, but mirroring a credible record across hundreds of sock puppets multiplies the stake and labor cost, while slashing burns the bond of any identity caught cheating. An ivory-tower registry alone cannot stop this — only the bond makes mass forgery unprofitable, because the attacker must pay for every mirror identity they spin up.
